title: The overlay: status pill, task cards, multi-monitor, desk view

findings.title: Status pill is pinned at top-centre and covers the control Ember is typing or clicking (address bar, ribbon tabs)
findings.scenario: The pill shows whenever Ember drives the keyboard or mouse ('Using your keyboard: press a key or move the mouse to take over', 'Using your mouse: move it to take over', 'Waiting until you stop using…'). It sits at a fixed top:40px, centred, 290-455 px wide and 48 px tall, and nothing moves it for the ring. In a maximised browser the address bar (Chrome/Edge on Windows, Safari/Chrome on macOS, Firefox on GNOME) is exactly at y 40-90, so while Ember types a URL the pill hides the middle of the address bar and the ring around it, and the user cannot watch what is being typed. Same for ribbon/menu tabs at top-centre in Office and similar. The pill is painted after the ring in DOM order, so it wins.
findings.evidence: Rendered the built overlay (harness.mjs, s7.mjs) with focus={x:260,y:48,width:920,height:32} over a mock address bar: the pill sits on top of the ring and hides the centre of the bar (s7-pill-over-url.png). Measured pill rect at 1366 and 1920 wide: y=40, h=48, w=290/455/390 depending on the text. Code: styles.css:10-11 (top:40px; left:50%), no z-index on .status or .focus; main.ts overlay never positions the pill relative to state.focus.
findings.fix: Position the pill in onState (app/renderer/overlay/main.ts) from the focus rect: when the ring (padded) intersects the pill's rect, move the pill to the bottom-centre above the taskbar/dock (or next to Ember), else keep the top. Also give .focus a higher z-index than .status so the ring is never under the pill.

findings.title: Task cards (and the handle) are drawn over the ring, the target control and Ember when the control is in the bottom-right corner
findings.scenario: The card stack is a 270 px column at the bottom-right above the handle (z-index 3); the ring has no z-index and Ember's canvas is z-index 1. When the control Ember works on or asks about is in that column (a fixed chat widget or cookie 'Accept' button at the bottom-right of a web page, a status-bar control, a 'Next' button in a full-screen wizard), Ember flies beside it with besideControl() which ignores the cards, and the card for that very task covers the control, the ring and most of Ember. 'May I click Next?' is asked about something the user cannot see; 'show me where' guides point at nothing.
findings.evidence: Rendered a 'Next' control at (1210,620) with one running task and the question bubble at 1366x768: the card hides the control, the ring and Ember is mostly under it (s6-under-card.png). Code: styles.css:23 z-index:3 vs .focus (styles.css:84) auto and #stage z-index:1; follow.ts besideControl() has no avoid rect; overlay.ts setState parks Ember at besideControl(f,…) only.
findings.fix: When state.focus (padded) intersects the card stack rect, collapse the stack to a single 'N tasks, Stop' chip or move it to the opposite corner; draw .focus above .tasks; pass keepOff() into besideControl so Ember never parks under the cards.

findings.title: Multi-monitor: 'keep off the cards' rectangle is the union of every display's cards, so Ember cannot follow the cursor over a wide band while any card shows
findings.scenario: Task state is broadcast to every overlay and each display draws its own card stack (the handle is on the primary only; other displays place the cards at bottom:80px,right:12px) and reports it through setCards. keepOff() merges the handle and all those rects into one global bounding box. With a second monitor to the left/right the box is a ~190 px tall strip across both displays; with one above the other it is a ~280 px column through both. followTarget then pushes Ember above that box whenever it overlaps. Example: secondary display to the left, any card on screen (even a 'Done' card for 15 s or a failure for 60 s), cursor at the bottom of the primary display: Ember sits 117 px above the cursor, nowhere near the cards at the right edge. With stacked monitors Ember jumps to the top edge when the cursor is in the right 300 px of the lower display.
findings.evidence: Simulated OverlayManager.tick() under vitest with two 1920x1080 displays (secondary at x=-1920), cards at x>=1630 (primary) and x -282..-12 (secondary), handle bottom-right, cursor (900,1000): Ember settles at y=854 with cards vs y=971 without; with the cursor on the secondary display it is unaffected (test removed after running). Code: overlay.ts:190-201 keepOff(), used at :150 and :354; renderer reports per display at main.ts(overlay renderer):228.
findings.fix: Make keepOff display-aware: for the display nearest the cursor use only the handle and the cards of that display's overlay (and clip them to that display's work area) instead of one global union.

findings.title: A second copy of the bubble appears on the neighbouring display when Ember is within ~2x its size of the seam
findings.scenario: isHere() accepts an Ember up to size*2 (120 px at the default size) outside the overlay's bounds so a straddling body is drawn on both displays. showBubble reuses that same test (line 435), so with Ember 30 px inside display B, display A also draws the bubble, clamped against its right edge, with live buttons. Moving the cursor across the seam while an answer or question is up (or parking by the seam) shows the bubble twice; a question shows two sets of Allow / Not now.
findings.evidence: Rendered two overlay pages with bounds {0,0,1440,900} and {1440,0,1440,900} and Ember at global x=1470: both pages report a visible bubble; stitched crop shows two identical bubbles at the seam (s9-seam.png).
findings.fix: Show the bubble (and body rect) only on the overlay whose bounds contain Ember's centre (or its anchor point); keep the wider margin only for the character canvas.

findings.title: A queued task's card shows the purple 'Needs you' question mark although nothing is needed from the user
findings.scenario: TaskManager.publish maps a queued task (more than 2 running, maxRunning=2) to status 'waiting'. The overlay (and the handle card) draw 'waiting' as the purple 'Ember asks you' question symbol with the screen-reader word 'Needs you: ', next to the detail 'Waiting to start'. A user with three tasks sees a purple question mark and is told by a screen reader that the task needs them, when it is simply in line.
findings.evidence: tasks.ts:292 status: t.status === 'queued' ? 'waiting'; overlay main.ts:236 STATE_WORD.waiting = 'Needs you: '; ember.css [data-status='waiting'] uses --sym-waiting (question) in --purple; DESIGN.md calls this symbol 'waiting for you'. Rendered card 'Tidy the desktop' with a purple '?' and 'Waiting to start' (s1-light.png). Same mapping in handle/main.ts:66.
findings.fix: Add a 'queued' status (neutral clock/dots symbol in grey, SR word 'Waiting its turn: ') and keep 'waiting' for tasks that really wait for the user.

findings.title: The handle pill says 'Ready' while tasks are running when no bubble is on screen
findings.scenario: An answer bubble times out (or a guide step ends) while a background task is still working. The task card above the handle says 'Working…' but the pill directly under it reads 'Ready' because its line is s.status ?? (bubble title/text || s.idle || 'Ready') and s.idle never accounts for tasks. The user gets two contradicting messages about whether Ember is busy.
findings.evidence: Rendered the handle page (s11.mjs) with state {bubble hidden, tasks:[{status:'running'}], idle:'Ready'}: the line reads 'Ready'. Code: handle/main.ts:123; main.ts:1523 sets idle only from agent status.
findings.fix: In the non-fallback branch, when any task is running or queued and nothing else is to be said, show 'Working on 1 task…' / 'Working on 3 tasks…'.

findings.title: Stop gives no immediate acknowledgement: the card keeps saying 'Working…' with a live Stop button until the worker unwinds
findings.scenario: Pressing Stop on a running card only sends the IPC; TaskManager.cancel() aborts the worker but publishes nothing until run() returns (it must wait for the session to go idle and tools to end). The user sees no change, cannot tell if the press landed, and may press again or reach for the kill switch.
findings.evidence: overlay main.ts:344 onPress handler only calls api.bubbleAction; tasks.ts:140-146 cancel() calls abort.abort() for a running task without setting task.detail or calling publish(); the card is only updated by finish(). Latency of worker unwinding not measured here.
findings.fix: On press, immediately set the card to a 'Stopping…' state (disable the button, change the detail) in the renderer, and have cancel() set task.detail='Stopping…' and publish().

findings.title: Polish: scrolling stack clips the card shadows into a hard-edged grey slab; finished cards jump to the top with no motion
findings.scenario: When the stack scrolls (many running/queued tasks) overflow-y:auto clips the 34 px card shadows at the container edge, leaving a visible rectangular grey halo with hard edges beside and between the cards over light apps. Separately, a task that finishes is re-ordered to the top group (stackOrder) and cards are added or removed with no exit or reorder animation, so a card the user is looking at disappears and its result reappears at the other end of the stack.
findings.evidence: Rendered 6 running cards at 1366x768 with real scrollbars (s2b.mjs): s2b.png shows the grey slab around the stack. Code: styles.css:26 .tasks.scroll overflow-y:auto with .task using --glass-depth shadows; stack.ts stackOrder moves ended cards first; main.ts renderTasks replaceChildren without FLIP.
findings.fix: Pad the scroller (padding 0 14px 40px with negative margin) so shadows are not clipped or drop the outer shadow in .scroll; animate reorder/removal (FLIP or a 150 ms fade) with Calm/Reduce Motion respected.

findings.title: Polish: Stop is the smallest, same-weight control on the card; long task details are not clamped
findings.scenario: Stop (the safety control) is a 24 px, 12 px-text capsule, styled identically to Close, so a stack of ended and running cards has indistinguishable buttons. Card details are unclamped: a finish_task summary may be 400 characters (a ~295 px tall card at 270 px wide) and the worker's fallback lastAnswer has no limit, so a long message makes one card fill the stack and fold the others into '+N more'.
findings.evidence: Measured card heights (s14.mjs): 179-char summary = 187 px, 343-char = 295 px; with a 2000-char detail all other cards fold and the card is taller than the screen (s5-long.png). styles.css:71 min-height 24px for both Stop and Close; worker.ts:1356 lastAnswer fallback unbounded, finish_task schema max 400.
findings.fix: Give running cards' Stop a 28 px height or an accent/red tint; clamp .task span to 4 lines with the full text in the bubble or on hover; clamp detail length in TaskManager.finish().

findings.title: Polish: the OS 'reduce motion' preference is read once at start for Ember's follow spring
findings.scenario: o.systemReducedMotion = sys.a11y.systemReducedMotion() runs once in makeOverlay(). If the user turns the OS animation setting on or off while Ember runs, the renderer (media query) follows live but Ember's spring in main keeps the old overshoot/critical damping until a restart or compositor change.
findings.evidence: main.ts:1222 is the only call site; overlay.ts:347 uses the cached flag every tick while the renderer reacts to matchMedia changes (overlay main.ts:100-103).
findings.fix: Re-read systemReducedMotion() when the settings change or every few seconds (it is a gsettings call on Linux, so keep it throttled), or have the renderer report its media-query state to main.

findings.title: Desk 'Take over' mode sends every key, Tab included, to the desk; the way out (Ctrl+Alt+End) is not exposed to assistive technology
findings.area: Desk window: No Keyboard Trap advisory (WCAG 2.1.2)
findings.scenario: A screen-reader user activates Take over and focus moves to the picture. All keys including Tab and Escape now go to the desk. The only way back is Ctrl+Alt+End, written in the header's visible hint, but the focused element is an image named only 'What Ember is doing on its desk' and has no description. The user is not told how to leave.
findings.evidence: AX tree in control mode (askdesk.mjs): image 'What Ember is doing on its desk' focusable, with no description; the hint is a StaticText in the banner. img.tabIndex=0 at desk/main.ts:45 even when not taken over.
findings.fix: Give #screen aria-describedby pointing at #hint, or set its alt/aria-label to 'Ember's desk. Your keys go to the desk. Press Ctrl+Alt+End to hand back' while control is on, and use a live region to say 'You have the keyboard on the desk'.
